notes:
BROWSER CHECK, 21 Oct 2026: opening https://rnli.org/news-and-media/rss in a real browser (the desktop app's built-in browser, normal browser user agent) does not return a feed or a 403; the site redirects to its own ASP.NET error handler, /errors/error?aspxerrorpath=/news-and-media/rss, titled 'An error has occured'. So the 403 the watch sees is not a user-agent refusal of a live feed: the path is dead for browsers too, and the feed should be treated as withdrawn. Proposed outside this bundle: set the rnli-news source to enabled:false in watch/sources.json with a note, and keep the task open only for the question of whether any other RNLI feed exists. What was found. No RSS or Atom feed is advertised anywhere on rnli.org that could be opened: the News and media listing (7,313 items, newest 19 Oct 2026) has no feed link element, the 'Latest lifeboat launches' page is an HTML list of 10 launches from the last 48 hours (crew pager system) with no feed or API, the press-enquiries page offers only social accounts, and neither sitemap nor robots.txt names a feed. The address the watch uses, https://rnli.org/news-and-media/rss, has answered HTTP 403 on all 36 watch runs since 15 Oct 2026 and was refused to the fetch tool here too (error type robots_disallowed, HTTP status not shown); sibling guesses /rss and /news-and-media/rss.xml give a client error. The Wayback 'available' API reports a single status-200 capture of /news-and-media/rss from 27 May 2022 and none since, so a feed (or at least a page) may have existed at that address in 2022 and later been removed or blocked; the capture could not be read from here. Acceptance points: a working feed address with newest-item date was NOT found; the headers that work could NOT be determined; the terms-of-use point IS covered, hence 'partial'. The feed question remains open, so if this bundle is accepted the reviewer may want --keep-open.

User-agent question. WebFetch cannot set custom headers, so the watch's UA (lifesavinglab-watch/1.0 with a site and contact address) versus a browser UA was not tested; this is stated plainly. Indirect evidence only: the fetch tool, which is also a non-browser client, read /news-and-media, robots.txt, the launches page, the terms page and the press page without trouble, so rnli.org is not refusing every non-browser client; the refusal looks path-specific. robots.txt disallows /cdn-cgi/ and the __cf_chl_tk / __cf_chl_rt_tk query parameters, which are Cloudflare paths and challenge tokens, so the site is very likely fronted by Cloudflare, whose bot rules commonly return 403 or a challenge page to unfamiliar user agents. That is an inference, not an observed status line.

Terms of use as stated by the site. robots.txt: one 'User-agent: *' block, no Crawl-delay, no named bots, no AI/automated-access policy; the only feed-related rule is 'Disallow: /*?feed=' (query string only) and /news-and-media/rss is not disallowed. Terms and conditions (last updated 15 November 2019): Term 7.2 permits printing and downloading extracts for personal non-commercial use; Term 7.3 says no other use may be made without written permission; Term 11.2 allows linking but not replication; nothing is said about bots, crawling, feeds or syndication. The watch stores only links, dates and hashes, not article text; whether that fits Term 7.2/7.3 is for the reviewer.

Suggested action (not done, outside the bundle): set rnli-news to enabled:false in watch/sources.json with a note, as was done for the USCG sources, until a person with a browser confirms an address. Figures seen but deliberately not added as rows: '7313 results' is a count of news items, and the launches page prints two different daily-aid averages ('an average of 23 people a day' and '122 people aided by our crews every day on average'), neither of which is a drowning figure or part of this task. No existing ledger row was touched; the only RNLI row in the ledger is rnli-lives-saved.
